- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and model shows gradual upward trend, reduce forecast slope; price may not rebound as expected.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment or price, model often overcorrects — cap upward momentum after peak; avoid overshoots in bullish phases.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model tends to underpredict downside — adjust downward bias by 5–10% of recent range.
- In high-event periods (e.g., >15 events/30d), model often fails to capture volatility — increase forecast volatility (±2–3% of mean) to reflect event-driven noise.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to drift toward historical mean — apply mean reversion only if price is >1.5σ above mean; otherwise, maintain trend.
- For multi-day event sequences (e.g., 3+ consecutive auctions), model often underestimates cumulative impact — add 1–2% cumulative adjustment per event to forecast.
- If sentiment is bullish but price is falling, model may misread sentiment — reduce forecast slope if sentiment >0.67 but price is trending down.
